framing: When candidate data passes 100K records, search and reporting become product problems—not just database queries.
challenge: The platform had to support candidate intake, pipeline search, assignment, interviews, AI-assisted evaluation, and regional reporting across more than 100,000 Postgres records, while keeping different role views safe and usable.
ownership: Product engineer for the candidate data and hiring-operations surface.
Built intake, pipeline, search, reporting, interview, and evaluation flows across Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Redis.
Owned the operational path: migrations, scheduled follow-ups, inactive-assignment checks, Docker Compose, NGINX, PM2, backups, and recovery steps.

decisions.title: Replace offset pagination at the point of failure
decisions.body: Swapped offset pagination for cursor pagination once the table passed 100K rows and offset queries started slowing down.

decisions.title: Precompute dashboard reads
decisions.body: Used materialized views for dashboard aggregation instead of hitting live tables for every load.

decisions.title: Protect access at the server boundary
decisions.body: Authentication and role checks protect CEO, manager, recruiter, national, and regional views before operational data reaches the interface.

decisions.title: Make AI a structured starting point
decisions.body: Added a Gemini-based summary generator that gives recruiters a structured evaluation to start from instead of a blank notes field.

evidence: Targeted indexes, cursor-based access, caching, and virtual scrolling keep large candidate result sets usable.
Dashboard aggregation uses materialized views rather than querying live tables on every load.
The product includes separate migrations, backups, recovery steps, and a deployment path using Docker Compose, NGINX, and PM2.
Recruiter time-saved and latency metrics are not published here, so none are inferred.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the product surface, the local engineering record, and resume-backed implementation details. No private hiring or performance metrics are inferred.
